citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
On 25 June 26, a covered mouse had surgery and was identified on the post-op monitoring as having a slight abnormal
gait on day 3 and laboratory personnel did not contact Campus Vet Services (CVS). Over the next 3 days the mouse
continued to ambulate and was otherwise normal, but on day 7 the affected limb was observed to have a significant paw
injury. At that point CVS was contacted, the animal was assessed and provided veterinary care. The principal investigator
and the laboratory staff did not follow the facility guidelines for contacting the attending veterinarian with timely and
accurate information about this issue. A mechanism of direct and frequent communication is required so that timely and
accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.

In the cat room, three kittens contained in enclosures did not have identifiable elevated resting surfaces. The kittens were
temporarily housed in the enclosures for veterinary care, but still need to be provided with elevated resting surfaces in
accordance with the regulations. Each primary enclosure housing cats must contain an elevated resting surface adequate
for the animals in the enclosure, impervious to moisture and able to be easily cleaned and sanitized or easily replaced
when worn or soiled.
Corrected during inspection on 20 Aug 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Attending Veterinarian and IACUC staff.
Additional Inspectors:
KATHARINE FRANK, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
